land.text: Inishowen from c. 465 and Tyrone, Derry and Limavady from about 700, taken from the Ulaid
Tyrone and its neighbours: 'fled in 1607 in what became known as the Flight of the Earls'; the earls' lands were then declared forfeit (Plantations page)

capitals.name: Dungannon
capitals.note: 'Its main capital was Dungannon, though kings were inaugurated at Tullyhogue Fort.' The page gives no years for either seat.

correction.text: Inishowen: 'The territory of Eoghan mac Neill was initially based in Inishowen' (a 28 km circle)

keyframe_review.note: [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Starts as Inishowen only (the whole of Tyrone, Derry and Limavady from 465 double-filled 23 H3 cells with ulaid's keyframe, which holds the land west of the Bann until the 8th century). New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Tír Eoghain. 'The territory of Eoghan mac Néill was initially based in Inishowen'; the page does not date the spread into Tyrone or later growth, so one shape stands for the whole life. The Armagh part belongs to the Airgíalla shape; the Raphoe area is 'noted separately' and has no extent.

correction.text: 'parts of present-day County Tyrone, County Armagh, County Londonderry and County Donegal' (drawn as Tyrone, Derry, Limavady and a 28 km circle for Inishowen; the Armagh and Raphoe parts are left out)

keyframe_review.note: [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] From 700 Tyrone, Derry and Limavady join Inishowen (gain from ulaid, ledger 700): the Ulaid page says 'By the 8th century the territory of the Ulaid shrunk to east of the Bann'; the Tir Eoghain page says the territory 'expanded out from there under his descendants' without a year. 700 is a bridge. New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Tír Eoghain. 'The territory of Eoghan mac Néill was initially based in Inishowen'; the page does not date the spread into Tyrone or later growth, so one shape stands for the whole life. The Armagh part belongs to the Airgíalla shape; the Raphoe area is 'noted separately' and has no extent.

ledger.note: c. 465: Eógan mac Néill, the first ruler (infobox 'c. 465: Eógan mac Néill (first)'; 'Established: 5th century'). 'The kingdom represented the core homeland of the Cenél nEógain people of the Northern Uí Néill.' The page starts the territory in Inishowen and gives no year for Tyrone, so the land beyond Inishowen is confidence 1. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] The founding now draws Inishowen only and names ulaid as counterpart (mirrors ulaid's 465 loss, confidence 1 there); Tyrone follows as a 700 gain from ulaid.

region.text: Tyrone, Derry and Limavady, west of the Bann, gained as the Cenel nEogain expanded from Inishowen

ledger.note: By the 8th century: 'the territory of the Ulaid shrunk to east of the Bann' (Ulaid page); the Tir Eoghain page says 'The territory of Eoghan mac Neill was initially based in Inishowen and expanded out from there under his descendants' and gives no year. Mirrors ulaid's 700 loss; a bridge, confidence 1.

region.text: Airgíalla (Armagh, Monaghan, Fermanagh and Louth), under Cenél nEógain dominance

ledger.note: 735 to 827: 'From 735 they fell under the dominance of the Cenél nEógain, and by 827 had become their vassals.' 827 is the vassal date; 735 the start of dominance.

region.text: Airgíalla, independent again under Donnchad Ua Cerbaill

ledger.note: Page silent on the end of the vassalage: the Airgíalla kingdom 'was at its peak in the 12th century, under king Donnchad Ua Cerbaill' (reign 1130-1168/9), so 1130 is a bridge (confidence 1).

region.text: Ulster, where Hugh O'Neill led Tyrone against the Crown

ledger.note: 1593: Hugh O'Neill takes Tyrone and the Nine Years' War begins. 'In 1593, infirm and of old age, Turlough stood aside in Tyrone for Hugh O'Neill' (Tír Eoghain page); 'the Nine Years' War (1593-1603)' (Tudor conquest page), 'the only province that was completely outside English control' (Plantations page).

1603: Tyrone submits. The Nine Years' War 'forced Tyrone to submit in 1603, completing the Tudor conquest of Ireland' (Kingdom of Ireland page); Treaty of Mellifont signed 'mere days after the death of Elizabeth I' (Tudor conquest page).

region.text: Tyrone, forfeit after the Flight of the Earls

ledger.note: 1607: the earls flee. 'Fled in 1607 in what became known as the Flight of the Earls' (infobox 'Disestablished: 1607'); 'the rebel earls left Ireland in the so-called 1607 Flight of the Earls' and Chichester declared their lands forfeit (Plantations page). The Plantation of Ulster 'began in the 1610s'.

wars.name: Nine Years' War
wars.outcome: Hugh O'Neill's Ulster confederacy held out until 1603, when Tyrone submitted; the Treaty of Mellifont ended the war and 'by 1603 the entire country was under English rule'.
wars.note: The Tír Eoghain page names the war only as 'the Nine Years' War under Hugh O'Neill'; the dates are the Tudor conquest page's.

certainty.note: The page names counties, no frontier.

sources.title: Airgíalla
sources.note: 735/827 domination of Airgíalla by the Cenél nEógain; 12th-century peak.

sources.title: Tudor conquest of Ireland
sources.note: Nine Years' War dates, Treaty of Mellifont, whole island under Crown control by 1603.

sources.title: Plantations of Ireland
sources.note: Ulster outside English control, Flight of the Earls 1607, forfeiture.

sources.title: Ulaid
sources.note: 'By the 8th century the territory of the Ulaid shrunk to east of the Bann'; land lost to the Airgialla and the Northern Ui Neill.

notes: The page states the status as 'Túatha of Ailech (until 1185)' without a reason and says the Ailech split was in both the 12th and 13th centuries; the ruling house passed from the Meic Lochlainn to the Ó Néill. 'Following the Norman invasion of Ulster in 1177, Tír Eoghain had become the predominant power' (not a territorial event). Conn Bacagh O'Neill 'accepted and went to London in 1542, pledging allegiance to Henry VIII', after the 1541 invasion under Anthony St Leger and the Geraldine League of 1539: a vassalage to the Kingdom of Ireland that the page does not close with a date, so it is not in the ledger. The kingdom-of-ireland dossier has a 1603 gain of the Gaelic lordships including Tyrone, while this dossier ends in 1607 with the Flight of the Earls; the 1603-1606 overlap should be read as Tyrone under the Crown with an O'Neill earl. The 735 start of Cenél nEógain dominance over Airgíalla is on the Airgíalla page. The 'Tyrconnell' neighbour (Cenél Conaill) has no dossier. The page budget was three pages. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] After the review: the 465 shape is Inishowen only and Tyrone, Derry and Limavady are a 700 gain from ulaid (confidence 1, the pages give no year); the Dungannon capital (no years on the page) lies outside the 465-699 shape. The 1603-1606 overlap with kingdom-of-ireland is settled there: that dossier's whole-island keyframe now excludes this state's shape until a 1607 gain cp tir-eoghain. Gaps left: the Ailech overkingdom (status line 'until 1185', split '12th century' and '13th century' on the same page) is not represented; the 1130 vassal_end over airgialla is a bridge.
